# Generated files and downloads

Inspect deliverables and save a local copy.

Applies to: Both

## Find output

Work can create files as task deliverables. Use the Files area or project workspace to inspect the actual file before relying on the final message.


## Preview and download

Select a file to open its preview, then use Download. The Files preview can be truncated at 50 KB and displays that fact. Download the original when you need the complete content.


## Check the result

Open downloaded spreadsheets, documents, code, or other output in the relevant application. Confirm that requested sections and data are present. Generating a file does not guarantee factual or formatting correctness.


## Keep a copy

Download important deliverables before deleting the conversation. Export project is useful when a deliverable consists of multiple related source files.


## Request a useful deliverable

Name the file format and what it must contain before the task runs. “Create a CSV with date, vendor, amount, and category” is more actionable than “make a file.” For a document, specify the intended audience and required sections. For code, ask for the full project and instructions needed to start it.

When the task completes, check that an actual file exists in the Files area or workspace. A response containing code or a Markdown table is not automatically a saved downloadable artifact. If the file is missing, ask the agent to create the named deliverable explicitly in Work.


## Verify downloaded output

Download the file and open it in the relevant program. Check that it is the expected format, opens without repair prompts, and includes the requested content. For tabular data, inspect row counts and key values. For generated code, inspect the project structure and run the documented checks in an appropriate environment.

A preview is a convenience and can omit content. The Files preview explicitly indicates truncation at 50 KB where applicable. Download the original before concluding that later rows, paragraphs, or source code are absent. Conversely, a good-looking preview is not proof that the downloaded file has been tested in every external application.


## Keep related files together

Use Export project when a deliverable includes several files with relative paths, imports, or assets. Downloading only the main source file can leave it unusable without the rest of the project. Keep any generated README or start instructions with the export so another person can reproduce the result.

Before deleting a conversation, retain the output outside OwnCMD. If a download fails, check the task and selected path, reload the saved conversation, and capture the displayed error. Do not replace a failed file link with a guessed path. If the task generated the wrong format or incomplete data, request a corrected artifact and review the replacement rather than relying only on an apologetic text response.
